title: Uniform amplitude on the constructible Serre coproduct closure over a Noetherian base
statement: Fix universes u and u+1, a prime ell, a field k in universe u with ringChar(k) different from ell, schemes Z,Y in universe u, a morphism aY:Y→Spec(k), a Noetherian Y, and a proper p:Z→Y. Let Λ be a commutative condensed ring object, with its specified multiplication, having IsEllAdicFinitenessCoefficient ell Λ: a finite normed Q_ell extension, the induced ring of integers of a finite embedded extension, the finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure, or the closed unit ball of a finite normed extension. Put Λ_T=p_T^*Λ and D_T=D(Mod(Λ_T)), with the actual total right derived functor Rp_* [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Constructibility means stratified local finite presentation [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The coefficient certification is the four-constructor class in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.RingObjects.Condensed.FinitenessCoefficient, with its monoid-object index, rather than a new coefficient construction. Let P_Z be the least replete class of Λ_Z-module objects containing the constructible modules and closed under kernels, cokernels, extensions and coproducts indexed in universe u+1. There exists an integer d such that for every M in P_Z, Rp_*(M[0]) has zero cohomology in all degrees greater than d. The bound is independent of M. No finite-type or separatedness assumption is imposed on aY, and k may have characteristic zero.

source.place: The amplitude clause, and the final passage from constructible sheaves to their filtered colimits; proper Noetherian specialization of Bhatt--Scholze 6.7.2 and 6.8.15.

proof.text: Properness and quasi-compactness of the Noetherian target give one finite bound r for geometric fibre dimensions. Work locally on a finite affine cover of Y; finitely many generators for affine charts of the proper morphism give such a bound, stable under field extension.

Apply the proper torsion cohomological-dimension theorem to the reductions of constructible integral lattices. The torsion bound is 2r. Integral proper pushforward is derived complete; its Milnor sequence gives the uniform bound 2r+1. For rational coefficients invert ell. For the algebraic closure descend finite local presentations to finite coefficient fields, then pass to the filtered colimit. The bound is unchanged by coefficient isomorphisms and by finite coefficient extensions. This is the proper case of Bhatt--Scholze 6.7.1--6.7.2 and 6.8.15, so no excellence or finite-type structure map to k is needed. To compare an abstract finite normed extension E with the embedded presentation, choose a Q_ell-embedding into the algebraic closure; uniqueness of the extended absolute value makes it isometric. It identifies the unit ball with the induced valuation ring, and continuous-function sheaf functoriality transports the coefficient ring and all module-object functors. This covers the explicit unit-ball constructor too.

Over these coefficient rings, constructible module objects form a coherent abelian subcategory on a Noetherian scheme. Its ambient filtered-colimit closure is replete and closed under kernels, cokernels, extensions and coproducts. Hence it contains the Serre coproduct closure. Bounded-below qcqs continuity commutes higher direct images with those filtered colimits, extending the bound from constructibles to their ind closure. Restrict it to P_Z. Empty fibres and zero modules satisfy the same bound.

theorem properLowerStar_uniformBound_ellAdic
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1})
    [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ] [IsEllAdicFinitenessCoefficient ℓ Λ]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ ℓ)]
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsNoetherian Y]
    (p : Z ⟶ Y) [IsProper p] :
    ∃ d : ℤ, ∀ M, constructibleCoproductClosure Λ Z M →
      (R((p)_*⟦Λ⟧).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M)).IsLE d
